summary: Tested the Episode target_date feature end-to-end: backend validation + planner sync (8 pytest tests), and a frontend smoke flow (login -> New Episode -> Save without generating -> verify episode page, Planner, Dashboard, cleanup). 8/9 backend tests pass; 1 fails exposing a real bug in the spec implementation. Frontend new-episode flow with target date works correctly.

critical.issue: Spec says deleting an episode should also delete its plan_items, but backend/episodes.py:delete_episode only removes the episode. Verified via test_delete_episode_removes_plan_items: linked plan_item is left behind (orphan with episode_id pointing at a non-existent episode; hydration returns 'episode': null). This leaves ghost chips on the Planner.

verified_flows: POST /api/episodes with target_date 'bad' -> 422 (validated by regex pattern)
POST /api/episodes without target_date -> 200 and NO plan_item created
POST /api/episodes with target_date -> plan_item created with same date, title, episode_id link (exactly 1)
PUT /api/episodes/{id} changing target_date -> single plan_item moves to new date (no duplicate)
PUT /api/episodes/{id} clearing target_date -> plan_item persists with date=None (Unscheduled)
PATCH /api/plan/{id} changes date -> unpublished linked episode's target_date is updated
PATCH /api/plan/{id} changes date on a PUBLISHED linked episode -> episode's target_date is NOT changed (good)
Frontend: data-testid intake-target-date-input present (type=date), hint 'Adds it to the Planner' shown, label 'Target publish date' shown
Frontend: After Save without generating, episode page renders data-testid episode-target-date with formatted date e.g. 'Wednesday, December 15, 2027'
Frontend: Planner page contains the new episode (chip + 'Episodes in progress' sidebar); Dashboard contains the episode in Upcoming.
action_items: FIX: In backend/episodes.py:delete_episode, add `await db.plan_items.delete_many({"episode_id": ep_id})` before/after the episode deletion. Then re-run /app/backend/tests/test_target_date.py::test_delete_episode_removes_plan_items to confirm.
critical_code_review_comments: episodes.delete_episode is missing the plan_items.delete_many that the spec explicitly promises.

planner.create_plan rejects linking an episode that already has a plan item (400). The 'Start episode from idea slot' flow depends on the frontend converting the pre-existing idea plan item (no episode_id) into a linked one or deleting it before create -- backend alone cannot dedupe. Please verify the frontend handler patches the existing plan item with episode_id/title rather than POSTing a second one (otherwise two plan items for the same date will exist).

episodes.sync_plan_date on episode UPDATE only triggers when target_date changed. If title/scripture/themes change, the linked plan_item's title/topic/primary_scripture/themes stay stale. Low priority but worth noting -- Planner chip can show the old title after a rename.
seed_data_creation: Tests create TEST_* episodes and plan_items and clean them up via fixtures/DELETE. One UI smoke episode created and deleted (DELETE 200). Note: due to the delete bug, UI smoke test leaves an orphan plan_item on 2027-12-15 titled 'TEST_UI_target_date_smoke'. Main agent should clean this up or let it clear when the delete fix is applied.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable test file: /app/backend/tests/test_target_date.py. All planner+target_date sync paths covered. The lone failing test is the DELETE episode -> cascade plan_items check. Also, one orphan plan_item exists in prod DB: title='TEST_UI_target_date_smoke', date='2027-12-15', episode_id points to a now-deleted episode. Delete it manually via DELETE /api/plan/{id} after fetching GET /api/plan.
rca of the issue: RCA: backend/episodes.py:delete_episode (lines 201-206) only calls db.episodes.delete_one and returns. The spec and companion code (sync_plan_date, _sync_episode_date) assume the plan_items collection is kept consistent with the episode lifecycle, but the delete path was never updated. Reproduce: POST /api/episodes with target_date -> GET /api/plan (shows item) -> DELETE /api/episodes/{id} -> GET /api/plan (item still there with episode set to null after hydration). Fix: add `await db.plan_items.delete_many({'episode_id': ep_id})` immediately after the successful db.episodes.delete_one call.
